deep.reconstruction:
The page is one block (p = 23) of a table of excluders (Excludentes) for Gauss's method of exclusion. The previous page holds the blocks for p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.

Meaning of the columns (inferred; verified on every row):
- Column A/f is a residue r = A/f mod p, running 1 to 22.
- Column f/A is its inverse r^{-1} mod p. Each pair multiplies to 1: 1·1, 2·12, 3·8, 4·6, 5·14, 7·10, 9·18, 11·21, 13·16, 15·20, 17·19 and 22·22 are all ≡ 1 (mod 23).
- For each residue x mod 23, the table classifies x by the value of r − x² (equivalently A − f x² divided by f).
- Middle column (no label): the x with r − x² ≡ 0 (mod 23). These exist only when r is a quadratic residue, as the roots ±√r: 1.22, 5.18, 7.16, 2.21, 11.12, 10.13, 3.20, 9.14, 6.17, 4.19, 8.15. Such x are admissible in either case.
- Top heading 'fgRp' (fg a residue mod p): 'Admittuntur' lists the x with (r − x² | 23) = +1, and 'Excluduntur' the x with (r − x² | 23) = −1.
- Bottom heading 'fgNp': the same two columns are read the other way round (Excluduntur / Admittuntur).

Purpose (my interpretation): it serves the method of exclusion of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae Art. 319–322. One wants x such that g·(A − f x²) is a square, as when solving M = f x² + g y² or finding representations of a number by a form. Mod p this requires fg·(r − x²) to be a square. So when fg R p, r − x² must be a residue or 0; when fg N p, it must be a non-residue or 0. Each excluding prime p then removes about half of the residue classes of x.

Computation behind the table (my reconstruction):
- Squares mod 23 for x = 0..11: 0, 1, 4, 9, 16, 2, 13, 3, 18, 12, 8, 6.
- Quadratic residues mod 23: Q = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 13, 16, 18}.
- For each r, Gauss computes r − x² and checks it against Q. The lists are symmetric under x ↔ 23 − x.
- Each non-residue row has 12 admitted and 11 excluded classes. Each residue row has 11 admitted, 2 zeros and 10 excluded.

Corrections on the page:
- A struck-out row between rows 3 and 4 (8 | 3 | ... | 10.13 | ...) is the r = 8 row written too early. It reappears correctly as row 8.
- In row 4, the first entries ('4 | 6') are written over other figures.
- The first figure of row 4's Excluduntur list is overwritten.

I recomputed all 22 rows by hand; every admitted, zero and excluded set agrees with the definition above.
errors: No arithmetic errors found: all 22 rows for p = 23 agree with Legendre-symbol computation of r − x² mod 23.

results.what: Exclusion table for modulus 23. For each r = A/f (mod 23), with inverse f/A, the residues x mod 23 are split by whether r − x² is a quadratic residue, zero, or non-residue. Admitted and excluded roles swap according to whether fg is a residue (fgRp) or a non-residue (fgNp) mod 23.
results.modern_name: Gauss's method of exclusion (sieve by quadratic residues, Legendre-symbol sieve) for representations by binary quadratic forms / factoring
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), Art. 319–322 and 329ff

deep.surprise_reason: This is a worked auxiliary table for Gauss's published method of exclusion (DA 1801). The tables are routine though careful computation, and the method is well known as his.

checkable.asserts: The f/A column is the inverse mod 23 of the A/f column.
Quadratic residues mod 23 used in the table.
